finding: The persisted per-round clean flag and its 'read as-is' fallback (plus the wholly-severity-less vs. mixed-round case split) are unearned stored surface: the flag is always reconstructable from the live surviving set. For a pre-release round, §3.1 defines clean as exactly 'zero findings survive', so any stored clean value equals (zero surviving). For a new wholly-severity-less round, §3.4's zero-surviving-first rule already returns clean when nothing survives, and §4.1's per-finding rule (missing severity = blocking) already returns not-clean via live recompute when anything survives. Both cases therefore reduce to the same live predicate — 'a severity-less round is clean iff zero findings survive' — so nothing needs to be persisted or read back, and the mixed/wholly distinction and 'empty means compatible' fallback add spec-and-storage surface (a stored key --record must write, --status must parse and reconcile) that feeds no decision the live recompute cannot make.
suggestion: Drop the persisted clean flag as a convergence input for severity-less rounds and state one derived rule: a round in which no surviving finding carries a severity is clean iff it has zero surviving findings (identical result under both blocking and all). This preserves pre-release back-compat (their recorded clean == zero-surviving by construction) while removing the stored flag, the read-as-is fallback, and the wholly-vs-mixed branch from §3.4 and Test 5.

finding: The wholly-severity-less fallback (§3.4) and Test 5 require a round 'recorded before this release' to be read by honoring 'that persisted clean flag, read as-is'. This assumes the pre-release .tp-review/ round record actually persisted a per-round clean boolean to fall back to. The spec never states this: the whole 'empty means compatible' upgrade rule is inoperable for genuinely-old rounds if the old convergence was computed on the fly from surviving-count and never stored a per-round flag. An implementer cannot build the pre-release fallback without knowing whether the field exists in the legacy schema, and if it does not, there is nothing to honor.
suggestion: State the implicit assumption explicitly: either assert that the pre-release record format already persists a per-round clean flag (name the field), and require it on every legacy round; or, if legacy rounds may lack it, define the fallback when the stored flag is absent (e.g. recompute clean = zero-surviving on the legacy round, matching pre-release severity-blind behavior), so the upgrade path is buildable without inspecting the old on-disk format.

finding: §3.4 (and Test 5) equate a round "recorded before this release" with a round that carries "no per-finding severity," routing both to the persisted-clean-flag legacy fallback. But tp's finding output contract has always mandated a `severity` field on every finding (`{"severity":"critical|high|medium|low",...}`, the same contract §7 strengthens for `role`). Genuinely pre-release recorded rounds therefore DO carry per-finding severity and would be handled by the live recompute path — not the severity-less fallback. The spec silently assumes a class of records (pre-release, severity-less) whose existence contradicts an existing tp invariant this release does not say it is changing, making the "recorded before this release" arm of the upgrade rationale dubious: either such records don't exist, or the severity contract wasn't always enforced in the stored round — the spec doesn't reconcile which.
suggestion: Reconcile §3.4/Test 5 with the finding severity contract: either (a) drop the "recorded before this release" framing and justify the severity-less fallback purely by the in-release "every finding omitted the severity field" case, or (b) if older `.tp-review/` records genuinely lack per-finding severity despite the live contract, state that explicitly (e.g. "records written by tp before severity was persisted per finding") so the upgrade arm rests on a documented schema gap rather than an unstated contradiction of the always-required severity field.
